cells.Definition / Overview: Highly contagious superficial infection (usually S. aureus)
cells.Clinical Presentation: Honey-colored crusted lesions, often on face, around mouth/nose.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Topical Mupirocin (Bactroban); oral Cephalexin if extensive.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Gentle cleansing with soap/water; avoid scratching.
cells.Patient Education: Good hand hygiene; keep lesions covered; avoid sharing towels or linens.

cells.Definition / Overview: Inflammation of hair follicle
cells.Clinical Presentation: Pustules centered on hair follicles; mild erythema, itching.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Topical Clindamycin, Mupirocin, or Benzoyl peroxide; oral Dicloxacillin for recurrent cases.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Warm compresses, antibacterial wash.
cells.Patient Education: Avoid tight clothing and occlusive products; change razors frequently.

cells.Definition / Overview: Inflammation of sebaceous glands and follicles
cells.Clinical Presentation: Comedones, papules, pustules, cysts on face, chest, back.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Mild: Benzoyl peroxide, Topical retinoids (tretinoin), Topical clindamycin. Moderate: add Doxycycline or Minocycline. Severe: Isotretinoin (REMS).
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Gentle cleansing twice daily, avoid picking.
cells.Patient Education: Educate about sun sensitivity, contraception w/ isotretinoin, 8–12 weeks for effect.

cells.Definition / Overview: Chronic facial flushing, erythema, and telangiectasias
cells.Clinical Presentation: Central facial erythema, papules, pustules, burning/stinging.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Topical metronidazole, Azelaic acid, Oral doxycycline for moderate cases.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Avoid triggers (heat, alcohol, spicy foods).
cells.Patient Education: Daily sunscreen; gentle cleansers; avoid corticosteroids on face.

cells.Definition / Overview: Chronic relapsing inflammatory skin disorder
cells.Clinical Presentation: Pruritic, scaly, erythematous patches; flexural surfaces.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Topical corticosteroids (hydrocortisone, triamcinolone); Antihistamines for itching; severe: Tacrolimus, Dupilumab.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Emollients multiple times daily; avoid hot showers, fragrances.
cells.Patient Education: Moisturize immediately after bathing; identify and avoid triggers.

cells.Definition / Overview: Inflammatory reaction from irritant or allergen exposure
cells.Clinical Presentation: Erythema, vesicles, pruritus localized to contact area.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Topical corticosteroids, Oral prednisone if severe; Antihistamines for itch.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Avoid offending agent, cold compresses.
cells.Patient Education: Wear gloves/protective gear; wash skin after exposure.

cells.Definition / Overview: Chronic autoimmune skin disease
cells.Clinical Presentation: Silvery plaques on extensor surfaces, scalp; may have nail pitting.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Mild: Topical corticosteroids, Vitamin D analogs (calcipotriene). Moderate-severe: Methotrexate, Adalimumab, Ustekinumab.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: UV light therapy, stress reduction, weight control.
cells.Patient Education: Adherence critical; avoid abrupt steroid withdrawal; moisturize regularly.

cells.Definition / Overview: Fungal infections (e.g., tinea corporis, pedis, cruris)
cells.Diagnosis: KOH prep shows hyphae; culture if unclear
cells.Clinical Presentation: Circular, scaly, pruritic patches; distinct borders.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Topical clotrimazole, Terbinafine; severe: Oral terbinafine or Fluconazole.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Keep area clean/dry, wear breathable fabrics.
cells.Patient Education: Treat all affected areas; avoid sharing shoes/towels.

cells.Definition / Overview: Fungal infection of nail plate
cells.Clinical Presentation: Thickened, discolored nails.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Oral terbinafine (first-line); Itraconazole alternative.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Keep nails short/dry; disinfect nail tools.
cells.Patient Education: Treatment may take months; monitor liver enzymes with terbinafine.

cells.Definition / Overview: Recurrent viral skin/mucosal infection
cells.Clinical Presentation: Painful grouped vesicles on erythematous base.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Acyclovir, Valacyclovir, Famciclovir.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Warm compresses for comfort; avoid triggers.
cells.Patient Education: Start antivirals early; avoid sexual contact during outbreaks.

cells.Definition / Overview: Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus along dermatome
cells.Clinical Presentation: Painful vesicular rash in dermatomal pattern; may precede pain (prodrome).
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Acyclovir, Valacyclovir, or Famciclovir within 72 hrs; pain: Gabapentin.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Cool compresses, rest, analgesics.
cells.Patient Education: Get Zoster vaccine (≥50 yrs); cover lesions; avoid contact with immunocompromised.

cells.Definition / Overview: Mite infestation of skin
cells.Clinical Presentation: Intense pruritus worse at night; burrows in webs of fingers.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Permethrin 5% cream (neck down, repeat in 1 wk); Ivermectin PO for resistant cases.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Wash bedding/clothes hot water; treat household members.
cells.Patient Education: Itching may persist post-treatment; avoid skin-to-skin contact until cleared.

cells.Definition / Overview: Infestation of hair/scalp/body
cells.Clinical Presentation: Itching, excoriations, visible nits near scalp.
cells.Pharmacologic Management: Permethrin 1% lotion, Ivermectin lotion if resistant.
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Wash clothing/bedding hot water; comb nits daily.
cells.Patient Education: Avoid sharing hats, combs, bedding; treat contacts.

cells.Definition / Overview: Mood disorder characterized by persistent low mood, anhedonia, and impaired daily functioning
cells.Diagnosis: Clinical (DSM-5 criteria); rule out medical causes
cells.Clinical Presentation: Depressed mood, loss of interest, fatigue, sleep/appetite changes, guilt, thoughts of death
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: SSRIs (Sertraline, Escitalopram, Fluoxetine); Alternatives: SNRIs (Venlafaxine, Duloxetine), Bupropion, Mirtazapine
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Interpersonal Therapy (IPT), lifestyle modifications
cells.Patient Education: Educate about medication adherence, onset of effect (4–6 weeks), monitor for suicidal thoughts, maintain routine and social support

cells.Definition / Overview: Chronic excessive worry and anxiety about multiple domains
cells.Clinical Presentation: Restlessness, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: SSRIs (Escitalopram, Paroxetine); Alternatives: SNRIs (Duloxetine, Venlafaxine), Buspirone, Benzodiazepines (short-term)
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: CBT, relaxation techniques, mindfulness, exercise
cells.Patient Education: Avoid abrupt discontinuation; use coping strategies; educate about delayed onset of effect for SSRIs/SNRIs

cells.Definition / Overview: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with concern about future attacks
cells.Clinical Presentation: Sudden intense fear, palpitations, chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, depersonalization
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: SSRIs (Paroxetine, Sertraline); Alternatives: SNRIs, Benzodiazepines (short-term), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Exposure therapy, relaxation training, breathing exercises
cells.Patient Education: Educate about recognizing triggers, slow breathing techniques, medication adherence

cells.Definition / Overview: Recurrent obsessions (intrusive thoughts) and/or compulsions (ritual behaviors)
cells.Clinical Presentation: Time-consuming obsessions, repetitive behaviors, distress
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: SSRIs (Fluoxetine, Fluvoxamine, Sertraline) at higher doses; Alternatives: Clomipramine, adjunct CBT (Exposure and Response Prevention)
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: CBT with exposure and response prevention
cells.Patient Education: Emphasize adherence, gradual exposure strategies, avoid avoidance behaviors

cells.Definition / Overview: Trauma-related disorder following exposure to life-threatening events
cells.Clinical Presentation: Intrusive memories, flashbacks, nightmares, hyperarousal, avoidance, negative mood
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: SSRIs (Sertraline, Paroxetine); Alternatives: SNRIs, Prazosin for nightmares
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Trauma-focused CBT, Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), mindfulness
cells.Patient Education: Encourage therapy participation, safe sleep, coping strategies for triggers

cells.Definition / Overview: Mood disorder with episodes of mania/hypomania alternating with depression
cells.Clinical Presentation: Mania: elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, distractibility; Depression: low mood, anhedonia
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: Mood stabilizers (Lithium, Valproate, Lamotrigine); Alternatives: Atypical antipsychotics (Quetiapine, Olanzapine), adjunct SSRIs (careful)
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Psychoeducation, routine sleep, monitoring mood
cells.Patient Education: Avoid alcohol/drugs, adherence critical, monitor for early mania signs, routine sleep and activity

cells.Definition / Overview: Chronic psychotic disorder with hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking
cells.Clinical Presentation: Hallucinations, delusions, disorganized speech/behavior, negative symptoms
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: Atypical antipsychotics (Risperidone, Olanzapine, Aripiprazole); Alternatives: Typical antipsychotics (Haloperidol), adjunct therapy for negative symptoms
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Social skills training, CBT for psychosis, supported employment
cells.Patient Education: Adherence to medication critical, monitor for side effects (metabolic, EPS), maintain social support

cells.Definition / Overview: Neurodevelopmental disorder with inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity
cells.Clinical Presentation: Difficulty focusing, impulsivity, restlessness, forgetfulness
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: Stimulants (Methylphenidate, Amphetamine salts); Alternatives: Atomoxetine, Guanfacine, Clonidine
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Behavioral therapy, organizational skills, parent/teacher interventions
cells.Patient Education: Educate on adherence, monitor growth/heart rate, behavioral strategies at home/school

cells.Definition / Overview: Difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep causing functional impairment
cells.Clinical Presentation: Trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, non-restorative sleep, daytime fatigue
cells.Pharmacologic Management: First-line: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I); Alternatives: Z-drugs (Zolpidem, Zaleplon), Ramelteon, short-term Benzodiazepines
cells.Non-Pharmacologic Management: Sleep hygiene, regular sleep schedule, limit caffeine/alcohol
cells.Patient Education: Avoid long-term use of sedative meds, reinforce sleep hygiene, track sleep patterns
